title: Balustrade and height-compliance boundaries (refer to building surveyor)
audience: Deck and fence workers who install or repair balustrades and must recognise compliance limits
learningOutcomes: Recognise the balustrade and height issues that are referred to a building surveyor or competent person.
Describe why a balustrade cannot be certified by the worker.
Record the referral and the height and gap measurements without making a compliance claim.

instruction.heading: Why balustrades are referred
instruction.body: A balustrade protects people from falling from height. For Class 1 housing, the NCC 2022 Housing Provisions call for a barrier wherever a person could fall 1 metre or more, and set the minimum barrier height at 1 metre above a deck or balcony floor, or 865 mm on stairs and ramps (no date shown). A worker can measure and record a balustrade, but the worker cannot certify that it complies. Refer balustrade height and gap questions to a building surveyor or other competent person, and do not state that a balustrade complies.

instruction.heading: Record the measurements and the referral
instruction.body: Record the measured height from the finished surface, the gaps through the balustrade, and the fixing method, with photographs and the date. Record which person the matter was referred to and what was asked. A Queensland government guideline dated March 2017 gives a barrier of at least 1 metre and a maximum gap of 125 mm for decks or balconies more than 1 metre above ground. It is older guidance, so check the current NCC rule before relying on it. Do not rebuild a balustrade to a target height without the referral outcome. A balustrade that is measured and referred is more useful to the owner than one that is changed without a record.

procedure: Measure the height from the finished surface, the gaps and the fixing method, and record the readings.
Photograph the balustrade with the measurement visible, with the date.
Do not state that the balustrade complies unless a competent person has confirmed it.
Refer the balustrade height and gap question to a building surveyor or competent person.
Record the referral, the person it was referred to and the question asked.
Hold any balustrade change until the referral outcome is recorded.

workedExamples.situation: An owner asks for a balustrade to be lowered to match a view, and says the new height will be fine.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not on the owner's statement alone. The height is a compliance question, and the worker cannot certify it. Measure and record the current height and gaps, refer the change to a building surveyor or competent person, and hold the change until the referral outcome is recorded.

equipmentAndPpe: Camera or phone for photographs with the measurement visible

commonErrors.error: Stating that a balustrade complies because it looks right.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the compliance question and state only what was measured.

commonErrors.error: Changing a balustrade height on the owner's instruction alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold the change until the referral outcome is recorded.

commonErrors.error: Not recording the measurements before any change.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the measurements and photographs before any work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Victoria registration threshold: domestic building work costing more than $10,000 needs registration as a registered building practitioner. Re-blocking, re-stumping or demolishing needs registration at any cost. Work above $10,000 needs that registration. This lesson does not give a registration or a building permit.

Barrier height and fall triggers: the NCC 2022 Housing Provisions require a barrier where a fall of 1 metre or more is possible, with a minimum height of 1 metre for decks, balconies and landings and 865 mm for stairs and ramps (no date shown). Compliance is confirmed only by a building surveyor or competent person.

Pool barriers are a separate regime. New South Wales requires a pool fence at least 1.2 metres high, measured from the finished ground level (updated 16 March 2026). Queensland requires a pool fence at least 1200 mm high, measured from finished ground level (updated 12 May 2025). These figures apply only where a balustrade forms part of a pool barrier, and must not be applied to decks by analogy.
Completing this lesson does not give a building surveyor, certifier or building licence, or authority to certify a balustrade.

qualityStandard: Measurements and photographs are recorded before any change.
No balustrade is stated to comply without competent confirmation.
The referral and its outcome are recorded before a height change is made.
documentationEvidence: Balustrade measurement record with height, gaps and fixing method
Photographs with measurement visible and date
summary: Balustrade height and gaps are compliance questions that the worker refers.
Record measurements and photographs before any change.
Do not state compliance without competent confirmation.

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner asks you to lower a balustrade to suit a view and says it will be fine. What is correct?
options: Measure and record the current height, refer the compliance question, and hold the change until the outcome is recorded
Lower it as requested, since the owner is paying for the work and has the final say on the design and the view
Lower it and say it complies with the standard, since the owner has said it is fine and will sign for it
Raise the balustrade instead, which keeps the view and also gives the owner the safety margin they want from the deck

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must a worker avoid stating that a balustrade complies?
options: Because balustrades are never compliant in any residential zone
Because compliance is a referred question that the worker cannot certify
Because the colour is wrong for the house and the deck finish
Because the owner pays for the certificate and expects it to be signed

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say the record of a balustrade should include?
options: A statement that the balustrade complies
The measured height from the finished surface, the gaps, and the fixing method, with photographs and the date
Only the owner's verbal description of the balustrade
The colour and the age of the timber

Balustrade compliance itself is referred to the building surveyor.
referencesAtEnd: Refer any balustrade compliance question to the building surveyor. Part 11.3 of the NCC 2022 Housing Provisions is the reference point for barrier heights. The Queensland deck, balcony and window safety guideline (March 2017) is older guidance and is not a compliance statement.
